_comment: LBNL FDD Chiller-Plant point -> CAMBER Role mapping. The plant has three chillers (_1/_2/_3) and three cooling towers; chiller 1 and tower 1 are the analysed units (the sensor-bias and tower-fouling faults are imposed on unit 1). Maps ONLY the plant-level points the runnable detectors need: chiller kW/ton (power + CHW loop) for chiller_efficiency, and the cooling-tower supply temp + wet-bulb for cooling_tower_approach. The dataset carries NO refrigerant-side points (evaporator/condenser approach, subcooling, superheat), so the refrigerant-side chiller-drift detectors stay synthetic-only -- see docs/VALIDATION.md. Dataset: LBNL Fault Detection and Diagnostics Datasets (CC-BY). NOTE the exported outdoor-temperature columns are swapped relative to the dataset's own inventory, which documents OA_TEMP as dry-bulb and OA_TEMP_WB as wet-bulb. The simulation's tower controller holds leaving water at max(wet-bulb + 8 F, 60 F): on the 210,661 minutes above the 60 F floor, CT_SW_TEMPSPT equals OA_TEMP + 8 to a median 0.28 F but OA_TEMP_WB + 8 only to 6.3 F. OA_TEMP_WB also exceeds OA_TEMP in 97% of rows (a wet-bulb cannot exceed its dry-bulb), and read as labelled the tower would cool water below wet-bulb half the time. The swap is corrected BEFORE this mapping is applied, as a 'fix' quirk on the lbnl-chiller catalog entry (camber/datasets/catalog.json), which swaps the two raw columns back; examples/lbnl_fdd/benchmark.py applies the same quirk. This mapping therefore maps the columns as labelled (OA_TEMP -> oat, OA_TEMP_WB -> wetbulb_temp) and must never be used on the raw export without that quirk. (Until 0.82.0 the raw columns were mapped as labelled with no correction; 0.82-0.85 baked the swap into this mapping.) The 'bypass' faults are on the single three-way valve that lets condenser water bypass the towers (inventory Table 1 / Figure 2), not on a tower. ALSO SWAPPED: the secondary chilled-water loop's CWL_SEC_SW_TEMP / CWL_SEC_RW_TEMP. As labelled, return is colder than supply in 98% of flowing hours and (supply - return) correlates +0.89 with CWL_SEC_LOAD; the primary loop (CWL_PRI_*) is labelled correctly. Not mapped here; the lbnl-chiller entry swaps them back with a second 'fix' quirk, so a mapping of the secondary loop may map them as labelled. 0.92 (#15): CDWL_SW_TEMP (the condenser-water loop supply, downstream of the tower-bypass mixing) maps to cond_entering_water_temp and TWV_CTRL (the three-way bypass valve command, 0-1) to cw_bypass_valve. Evidence: with TWV_CTRL <= 0.02 and a chiller running, CDWL_SW_TEMP - CT_SW_TEMP_1 has a median of 0.03 F (10-90%: 0.00-0.11 F) in the fault-free run and 0.01 F in the 65% tower-fouling run, but 23-47 F in the bypass leakage/stuck runs; the valve is on the condenser loop, not on a tower (inventory Table 1 / Figure 2). 0.97 (#82): the secondary chilled-water loop's lead pump speed CWL_SEC_PM_SPD_1 (0-1) maps to chw_pump_speed, and its differential pressure CWL_SEC_DP and setpoint CWL_SEC_DPSPT to chw_diff_press / chw_diff_press_sp, for the chw_pump_dp_reset rule (the workbook's pumping exercise). Evidence: in the fault-free run the pump speed sits at its 0.345 VFD floor in 33% of minutes and at or above 0.9 in 39%, and the DP setpoint is a constant 960.96 (no DP reset); in the secondary_chilled_water_pressure_bias runs the biased DP reading is the controlled variable, so it stays near its setpoint and the pump speed carries the fault. CWL_SEC_PM_STA_1 is not mapped: like CHL_STA_1 it is 1 in every row (an enable). The primary-loop setpoint CWL_PRI_SW_TEMPSPT stays unmapped.
